d.g: A long, narrow, deep inlet between cliffs.

fjord.e: Unadapted borrowing from Norwegian fjord, from Old Norse fjǫrðr, from Proto-Germanic *ferþu, *ferþuz (“inlet, fjord”), from Proto-Indo-European *pértus (“crossing”), from *per- (“to carry forth”) + *-tus (suffix forming action nouns from verb roots). Doublet of firth, ford, port, and fjard.

d.g: A rocky, barren plateau, especially in Scandinavia.
d.x: Almost every Norwegian farmer possesses some pasture-land high up in the fjeld, sometimes as much as twenty or thirty miles distant from his homestead.

fjeld.e: Borrowed from Danish fjeld. Doublet of fell.

d.g: a relatively small but very strong horse breed from the mountainous regions of western Norway.

fjord horse.e: Probably an anglicisation of Norwegian fjordhest.

d.g: A more or less open body of water in a coastal archipelago.
d.x: However, a variety of drowned glacial valleys called fjards have developed in the low-relief rocky coast of northern Sweden, having cross-sections with less steep walls and presenting some lateral terraces which may be confused with strandflats.

fjard.e: Borrowed from Swedish fjärd. Doublet of fjord, ford, port, and firth.
